description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and accuracy (ACC, y-axis) for five different model variants—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, and ROME—evaluated on long-tail biomedical knowledge editing tasks. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” spans from 0 to approximately 10⁴ on a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges linearly from 60% to 85%, with tick marks every 5 percentage points. The Base model (black line with circular markers) shows a steady, modest increase in accuracy from ~64% at co-occurrence 1 to ~71% at 10⁴. The FT model (blue line with downward-pointing triangles) starts at ~65.5% and rises to ~73%. The IKE model (red line with upward-pointing triangles) begins at ~67.5% and reaches ~75.5%. The MEND model (brown line with diamond markers) starts at ~70.5% and climbs to ~80%. The ROME model (green line with square markers) begins at ~74.5% and achieves the highest accuracy of ~83% at the highest co-occurrence number. All lines exhibit a generally upward trend, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the entire range.
